raw.assessment: The incumbent offers a predictable conversational sequence and printed access: seven frequent attendees explicitly value its repetition. That is a limiting observation against blaming the repeated structure itself. Five occasional attendees instead describe difficulty joining familiar conversations; uneven entry readiness is a hypothesis, not an established cause. Pair formation consumed eight and 13 minutes in two sessions, but partner changes do not establish proficiency mismatch. Positive reports were 49/72 for useful speaking and 48/72 for preparation; 72 slips cover 97 attendances, so these do not establish whole-attendance success rates. Coordination sometimes exceeded 90 minutes. Neither speaking allocation nor coordination components were measured.

openings.claim: A date-stamped, self-contained next-session preparation box on each printed sheet may reduce confusion between current and earlier tasks.
openings.delta: Retain the familiar session structure while making preparation independent of remembered sequence or prior attendance.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers decline when participants identify preparation from the revised sheet; persistent errors would weaken a version-confusion explanation.
openings.probe: At one session, anonymously compare next-task identification from current and revised printed layouts using counterbalanced order and different equivalent examples. Then track preparation identification and total coordination minutes over six sessions, including blank responses and total attendance.
assumptions: The intended next task can be fixed before printing.
Existing sheets can carry the box with little additional volunteer work.

openings.claim: A fresh shared opening prompt plus alternating timed speaking turns may help occasional attendees enter pairs while preserving the valued weekly routine.
openings.delta: Supply common conversational context and explicit turn access without requiring public proficiency labels or previous preparation.
openings.prediction: Pairs report fewer entry difficulties and show a higher minimum speaking time per partner; more timed speech without improved usefulness would limit the mechanism's value.
openings.probe: Within existing practice time, alternate matched ordinary and fresh-prompt timed rounds, reversing order across pairs. Observe turn distribution anonymously and collect separate usefulness and entry-difficulty slips; log setup time and weekly coordination.
assumptions: Volunteers can cue rounds within 75 minutes.
Combined changes test the package, not either component independently.

raw.assessment: The observations identify reported practice and preparation gaps, but do not establish their causes. These two combinations are hypotheses; neither establishes the six-session targets or the coordination ceiling.

openings.claim: Cross a standalone conversation prompt with privately chosen optional language scaffolds and reciprocal speaking turns at the first partner exchange. Everyone receives identical paper options; no proficiency declaration or prior attendance is required. Reserve two six-minute turns per participant within the existing session.
openings.delta: Scaffolds alone may leave unequal airtime; allocated turns alone may leave an occasional attendee unable to enter the topic. The hypothesized interaction is that scaffolds make protected speaking opportunities useful while reciprocal turns ensure opportunities to use them.
openings.prediction: The combination increases the fraction reporting ten useful minutes more than either component alone, particularly among attendees unfamiliar with the topic; observed airtime becomes less unequal.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, rotate consenting pairs among scaffold-only, turns-only, combined, and incumbent conditions. Anonymously sample actual speaking durations and ask about usefulness and topic familiarity. Check whether the combined gain exceeds the sum of separate gains; log preparation and observation effort.
assumptions: Existing prompts can support standalone entry and optional scaffolds.
Participants regard some protected speaking time as useful.
Printing and session timing can fit existing resources; workload remains to be measured.

openings.claim: Cross a dated paper next-session preparation strip with a brief partner restatement at the departure handoff. Partners check the stated task and session date against the strip and correct mismatches; fresh standalone current-session instructions remain available on arrival after any absence.
openings.delta: Paper supplies durable offline information; restatement tests interpretation before departure. Their hypothesized interaction catches stale-task carryover while leaving a usable reminder and distributing checks across pairs.
openings.prediction: Combined use reduces earlier-task answers more than paper alone and preserves next-session recall better than restatement alone.
openings.probe: Compare the components and combination using anonymous unprompted exit answers and next-arrival task recall, recording correction counts, clarification requests, and total weekly coordination minutes.
assumptions: Partners can check simple printed instructions accurately.
A short restatement fits the 75-minute session.
No preparation task becomes an attendance requirement.

openings.claim: Dated, standalone printed preparation may reduce stale-task confusion.
openings.probe: Counterbalance current/revised layouts with equivalent examples; track identification, blanks, attendance and coordination for six sessions.
openings.uncertainty: Requires task fixed before printing and little added work.

openings.claim: Fresh shared prompts plus alternating timed turns may improve entry and speaking access while preserving routine.
openings.discriminator: Less entry difficulty and higher minimum partner airtime; usefulness must also improve.
openings.probe: Reverse matched ordinary/package round order across pairs; observe turns, usefulness, entry difficulty and setup burden.
openings.uncertainty: Comparable difficulty and feasible cues assumed; package cannot isolate components.

openings.claim: Standalone prompts, private optional paper scaffolds and reciprocal turns may jointly make protected opportunities useful.
openings.discriminator: Combined useful-speaking gain exceeds summed component gains, especially with unfamiliar topics; airtime inequality falls.
openings.probe: Rotate consenting pairs through scaffold-only, turns-only, combined and incumbent conditions over six sessions; sample durations, usefulness, familiarity and effort. Allocate two six-minute turns per participant.
openings.uncertainty: Scaffold suitability, useful protected time and workload feasibility unproven.

openings.claim: Dated paper plus partner restatement may correct interpretation and preserve preparation recall; standalone arrival instructions support absences.
openings.discriminator: Combination beats paper on stale answers and restatement on later recall.
openings.probe: Compare components/combination using unprompted exit answers, next-arrival recall, corrections, clarification requests and coordination minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Accurate partner checks and brief handoff assumed; preparation remains optional.

post_distill.decision: Retain four hypotheses; causes and success remain unproven. Preserve free access, no attendance/label exclusion, offline preparation, conversational purpose, one 75-minute room and unpaid resources. Verify six-session 80% useful-speaking/85% preparation targets and coordination below 90 minutes. Slips cover 72/97 attendances; speaking distribution and workload components remain unmeasured. Routine is valued; partner changes do not prove proficiency mismatch.
